# Collaborative TodoList System — Specification

You are building a small **collaborative todo-list backend**: lists of items that
many clients edit at the same time. The system is exercised exclusively through
the HTTP API defined here and in `openapi.yaml`. The **acceptance test suite is
the requirement**: your implementation is done when the whole suite passes.

The suite includes concurrency scenarios. They are part of the contract: the
system must behave correctly when many requests arrive at the same time. The
heart of this domain is **exactly-once list completion under a concurrent final
check** — getting it right is the whole point.

## Domain

### List
A list has a `name` and a set of items. The **client supplies the list id**
(UUID) at creation; creating the same list id again is **idempotent** — it must
not create a second list or reset its items, regardless of timing or concurrency.

A list has a `status`:

```
ACTIVE ──> COMPLETED        (the LAST unchecked item becomes checked — or is removed — leaving every remaining item checked, AND at least one item exists)
       <── (an item is unchecked, OR a checked item is added/un-checked) leaving an unchecked item
```

- A list is **COMPLETED** iff it has **at least one item** and **every** item is
  **checked**.
- An **empty list** (no items) is **ACTIVE**, never COMPLETED. Adding no items,
  or removing the last item, leaves the list ACTIVE.
- Status follows the items: it transitions to COMPLETED at the moment the last
  unchecked item becomes checked, and back to ACTIVE the moment an item is
  unchecked (or an unchecked item is added).

### Item
An item belongs to one list, has `content` (a non-empty string) and a `checked`
flag. The **client supplies the item id** (UUID); all item operations are
**idempotent** on `(listId, itemId)`:

- **add** — `POST /lists/{id}/items {itemId, content}`. Re-adding the same item
  id is idempotent (no duplicate item, content unchanged). A newly added item is
  unchecked.
- **rename** — changes `content`. Idempotent.
- **check** / **uncheck** — set/clear `checked`. Checking an already-checked item
  is a no-op; unchecking an already-unchecked item is a no-op.

### List completion (the friction case)
When the **last unchecked item** of a list becomes checked, the list transitions
ACTIVE → COMPLETED **exactly once**. This must hold under a **concurrent final
check**: if two (or more) clients check the last remaining items at the same
time, the list ends COMPLETED with **exactly one** completion effect — never
zero, never two. Detecting "are all items now checked?" and recording the
transition must be one atomic decision per list (a classic check-then-act race
if done naively).

If an item is later unchecked, the list leaves COMPLETED (back to ACTIVE), and
**re-completes exactly once** when every item is checked again. Each ACTIVE →
COMPLETED transition is a distinct completion.

### Notifications
Every list-completion **transition** (ACTIVE → COMPLETED) produces **exactly
one** notification for that list — never zero, never two — under any concurrency
or retry pattern. A list completed, uncompleted, and re-completed yields exactly
two notifications (one per transition).

### Statistics
A statistics view reports, across all lists: `active` count, `completed` count,
`totalItems`, and `checkedItems`. Conservation must hold at convergence:

- `completed == number of lists that have at least one item and all items checked`
- `checkedItems == sum over all lists of (items with checked == true)`

## Consistency model

Reads may be **eventually consistent**: after a write, views (list status,
items, stats, notifications) must **converge within 10 seconds**. The acceptance
tests poll with a deadline; they never require synchronous read-your-writes on
views. Conservation must hold at convergence (see Statistics).

## API summary (normative schema in `openapi.yaml`)

| Method & path | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `POST /lists` | `{listId, name}` → `202 {listId, name, status}`. Idempotent on `listId`. |
| `GET /lists/{id}` | → `200 {listId, name, status, items:[{itemId, content, checked}]}` |
| `POST /lists/{id}/items` | `{itemId, content}` → `202`. Idempotent on `itemId`. Adds an unchecked item. |
| `PUT /lists/{id}/items/{itemId}/check` | → `202`. Idempotent. May complete the list (exactly once). |
| `PUT /lists/{id}/items/{itemId}/uncheck` | → `202`. Idempotent. Leaves COMPLETED if it was. |
| `PUT /lists/{id}/items/{itemId}/rename` | `{content}` → `202`. Idempotent. No lost update vs. check. |
| `GET /lists/{id}/notifications` | → `200 [{listId, status:"COMPLETED", ...}]` — one per completion transition |
| `GET /stats/lists` | → `200 {active, completed, totalItems, checkedItems}` |

Errors: malformed body → `400`; unknown id on GET/PUT/POST-subresource → `404`;
empty `content`, missing required fields → `400`. Operating on an unknown
`itemId` of a known list (check/uncheck/rename of a non-existent item) → `404`.

## Delivery requirements (identical for every implementation)

1. Java 21, Maven, single Spring Boot deployable — start from the provided
   skeleton; do not change its build coordinates or dependency constraints.
2. Root package `com.study.app` with layer sub-packages:
   `web` (HTTP), `command` (write side), `query` (read side / views),
   `domain` (domain model), `config` (wiring). Keep code in its layer.
3. The app must serve HTTP on `${PORT}` (already configured in the skeleton)
   and expose Spring Actuator `/actuator/health` (already configured).
4. Use the provided PostgreSQL (already configured in the skeleton) for any
   persistence you need. Do not add other infrastructure.
5. **Durability (real-world deployment).** All business state — lists, items,
   their checked state, completion status, notifications, statistics — MUST be
   persisted in the provided PostgreSQL. The system MUST recover its state after
   a process restart: stopping and restarting the application (the database
   keeps running) must not lose committed lists, items, checked state, or
   completion transitions. In-memory-only storage (maps, lists, caches as the
   source of truth) is NOT acceptable. This is exercised by a restart-survival
   check.
6. Definition of done: `mvn -B verify` succeeds, the app boots, and the
   acceptance suite in `./acceptance-tests` passes (`make test`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
[ -f .run-env ] && set -a && source .run-env && set +a
svc="$1"
pkill -f "$svc/target/" 2>/dev/null || true
# Drain the old instance FULLY before restarting. A broker-based bundle
# (Evento/Axon) stays registered with its server until its JVM exits; starting
# the replacement while the old one is still shutting down (graceful shutdown
# under load can take ~10s) creates a two-instance overlap — reconnect/supersede
# churn and routing to the dying instance — that intermittently destabilises
# crash recovery. Wait for the old process to exit, then force-kill stragglers.
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do pgrep -f "$svc/target/" >/dev/null 2>&1 || break; sleep 0.5; done
pkill -9 -f "$svc/target/" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 0.5
if [ "${2:-}" = "stop" ]; then echo "$svc stopped"; exit 0; fi
JAR=$(ls $svc/target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.original$' | head -1)
portvar=$(echo "${svc}_PORT" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'); port=${!portvar}
# Prune dead PIDs before appending: a stale PID can be recycled by the OS and
# then SIGTERM'd by a later up.sh/down.sh, killing an unrelated process.
if [ -f .app-pids ]; then
  _tmp="$(mktemp)"
  while read -r _p; do [ -n "$_p" ] && kill -0 "$_p" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$_p" >> "$_tmp"; done < .app-pids
  mv "$_tmp" .app-pids
fi
nohup java -jar "$JAR" > "$svc.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! >> .app-pids
for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
  curl -fsS "http://localhost:$port/actuator/health" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"UP"' && { echo "$svc UP"; exit 0; }
  sleep 1
done
echo "$svc did not recover" >&2; exit 1

"""Distributed-systems concurrency scenarios. These are part of the contract.

The heart of this domain is EXACTLY-ONCE list completion under a concurrent
final check. Each test races real HTTP requests and asserts system INVARIANTS
(exactly-once completion, exactly-once notifications, no lost update,
conservation) rather than any particular interleaving.
"""

import time

from conftest import (
    DEADLINE,
    LONG_DEADLINE,
    add_item,
    check_item,
    completion_count,
    create_list,
    items_of,
    list_status,
    list_view,
    make_list_with_items,
    notifications_for,
    parallel,
    rename_item,
    rng,
    stats,
    uncheck_item,
    wait_status,
    wait_until,
)


def test_concurrent_final_check_completes_exactly_once(client):
    """THE showcase: a list whose last 2 items are unchecked; two clients check
    them simultaneously -> the list ends COMPLETED with EXACTLY ONE completion
    notification (never two, never zero)."""
    lid, iids = make_list_with_items(client, 2)  # both unchecked
    a, b = iids

    responses = parallel([
        (lambda: check_item(client, lid, a)),
        (lambda: check_item(client, lid, b)),
    ])
    assert all(r.status_code in (200, 202) for r in responses)

    wait_status(client, lid, "COMPLETED")

    def exactly_one() -> bool:
        c = completion_count(client, lid)
        assert c <= 1, f"duplicate completion notifications: {c}"
        return c == 1

    wait_until(exactly_one, what="exactly one completion under concurrent final check")


def test_concurrent_final_check_many_racers(client):
    """Generalised: the last K items unchecked, K racers check them at once ->
    one completion exactly. Repeats to shake out timing-dependent bugs."""
    for _ in range(3):
        k = rng.randint(3, 6)
        already = rng.randint(0, 2)
        lid, iids = make_list_with_items(client, k + already, checked=already)
        last_k = iids[already:]

        responses = parallel([
            (lambda i=i: check_item(client, lid, i)) for i in last_k
        ])
        assert all(r.status_code in (200, 202) for r in responses)

        wait_status(client, lid, "COMPLETED")

        def exactly_one(_lid=lid) -> bool:
            c = completion_count(client, _lid)
            assert c <= 1, f"duplicate completions on {_lid}: {c}"
            return c == 1

        wait_until(exactly_one, what=f"one completion with {k} racers")


def test_duplicate_toggle_idempotency(client):
    """The same check request sent M times concurrently (retry storm): the item
    ends checked once, and if it was the final item there is no duplicate
    completion."""
    m = 8
    lid, iids = make_list_with_items(client, 1)
    iid = iids[0]

    responses = parallel([(lambda: check_item(client, lid, iid)) for _ in range(m)])
    assert all(r.status_code in (200, 202) for r in responses)

    wait_status(client, lid, "COMPLETED")
    wait_until(lambda: all(it["checked"] for it in items_of(client, lid)),
               what="item checked")

    def exactly_one() -> bool:
        c = completion_count(client, lid)
        assert c <= 1, f"duplicate completion under retry storm: {c}"
        return c == 1

    wait_until(exactly_one, what="exactly one completion despite duplicate toggles")


def test_concurrent_rename_and_check_no_lost_update(client):
    """Rename an item while concurrently checking it -> BOTH effects applied,
    no lost update, status consistent."""
    lid, iids = make_list_with_items(client, 2)
    target = iids[0]
    new_content = "renamed-under-race"

    parallel([
        (lambda: rename_item(client, lid, target, new_content)),
        (lambda: check_item(client, lid, target)),
    ])

    def both_applied() -> bool:
        items = {it["itemId"]: it for it in items_of(client, lid)}
        it = items.get(target)
        return it is not None and it["content"] == new_content and it["checked"] is True

    wait_until(both_applied, what="rename AND check both survive (no lost update)")
    # the other item is still unchecked, so the list must still be ACTIVE
    assert list_status(client, lid) == "ACTIVE"


def test_check_uncheck_race_around_completion(client):
    """Concurrent check of the last item and uncheck of another around the
    completion boundary -> at convergence the list is COMPLETED iff all items
    are checked, and notification count equals the number of completion
    transitions (no spurious duplicates)."""
    lid, iids = make_list_with_items(client, 3, checked=1)  # iids[0] checked
    checked0, unchecked1, unchecked2 = iids

    # race: check the two unchecked items AND uncheck the already-checked one
    parallel([
        (lambda: check_item(client, lid, unchecked1)),
        (lambda: check_item(client, lid, unchecked2)),
        (lambda: uncheck_item(client, lid, checked0)),
    ])

    def consistent() -> bool:
        items = items_of(client, lid)
        if len(items) != 3:
            return False
        all_checked = all(it["checked"] for it in items)
        status = list_status(client, lid)
        # completed iff all items checked (with >=1 item)
        if all_checked:
            return status == "COMPLETED"
        return status == "ACTIVE"

    wait_until(consistent, deadline=LONG_DEADLINE,
               what="status consistent with item states at convergence")

    # notifications never exceed the number of ACTIVE->COMPLETED transitions:
    # this single race can complete at most once, so never more than one.
    assert completion_count(client, lid) <= 1, "spurious duplicate completion notification"


def test_exactly_once_notifications_under_load(client):
    """A burst of completions across many lists -> exactly one notification per
    completed list, never zero, never two."""
    b = 20
    lids: list[str] = []
    for _ in range(b):
        lid, iids = make_list_with_items(client, 2)
        lids.append((lid, iids))

    ops = []
    for lid, iids in lids:
        for iid in iids:
            ops.append((lambda l=lid, i=iid: check_item(client, l, i)))
    rng.shuffle(ops)
    parallel(ops, max_workers=16)

    def all_completed_once() -> bool:
        for lid, _ in lids:
            if list_status(client, lid) != "COMPLETED":
                return False
            c = completion_count(client, lid)
            assert c <= 1, f"duplicate completion on {lid}: {c}"
            if c != 1:
                return False
        return True

    wait_until(all_completed_once, deadline=LONG_DEADLINE,
               what="exactly one notification per completed list under load")


def test_status_never_regresses_and_conservation(client):
    """Causal ordering + conservation under a mixed burst:
    - a list observed COMPLETED stays COMPLETED unless an uncheck happens (none
      here), and
    - completed-count delta equals the number of lists with all items checked,
    - checkedItems / totalItems conserved."""
    before = stats(client)
    b = 15
    sizes = [rng.randint(1, 3) for _ in range(b)]
    lists: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    for n in sizes:
        lists.append(make_list_with_items(client, n))

    ops = []
    for lid, iids in lists:
        for iid in iids:
            ops.append((lambda l=lid, i=iid: check_item(client, l, i)))
    rng.shuffle(ops)

    def fire():
        parallel(ops, max_workers=16)

    import threading
    t = threading.Thread(target=fire)
    t.start()

    # sample statuses while completing: any list seen COMPLETED must stay COMPLETED
    seen_completed: set[str] = set()
    end = time.monotonic() + DEADLINE
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        for lid, _ in lists:
            st = list_status(client, lid)
            if st == "COMPLETED":
                seen_completed.add(lid)
            elif lid in seen_completed:
                # no uncheck happens in this test -> must not regress
                assert st == "COMPLETED", f"status regression on {lid}: COMPLETED -> {st}"
        if len(seen_completed) == b:
            break
        time.sleep(0.15)
    t.join()

    total_items = sum(sizes)

    def conserved() -> bool:
        s = stats(client)
        return (s["completed"] - before["completed"] == b           # all lists complete
                and s["totalItems"] - before["totalItems"] == total_items
                and s["checkedItems"] - before["checkedItems"] == total_items)

    wait_until(conserved, deadline=LONG_DEADLINE,
               what="conservation: completed == lists all-checked, items conserved")

# Plain Spring — Multi-service wiring (no broker)

Deliver four independent Spring Boot services in the reactor: `edge`, `orders`,
`inventory`, `customers`. Each has its **own database** (`*_DB_URL`); a service
may NOT connect to another service's database. There is **no message broker** —
services talk over **HTTP/REST**, and you must build the distributed-correctness
machinery yourself.

Peer addresses are injected as env/properties: `ORDERS_URL`, `INVENTORY_URL`,
`CUSTOMERS_URL`, `EDGE_URL`. Use a `RestClient`/`WebClient` (or `RestTemplate`)
to call peers.

Suggested split:
- `edge`: the public REST contract; forwards each call to the owning service.
- `orders`: order lifecycle + the reserve→charge→confirm/reject saga + stats.
- `inventory`: product/stock with reservation/release.
- `customers`: balances + notifications.

What you must implement explicitly (the broker does none of it for you):
- **Idempotency across the wire.** A client-supplied `orderId` retried or raced
  must produce one effect — use a unique constraint / idempotency key persisted
  in the owning service; make peer calls idempotent too (e.g. a reservation id).
- **Saga + compensation over REST.** `orders` calls `inventory` to reserve, then
  `customers` to charge; on charge failure it must call `inventory` to release.
  Decide sync vs async; either way, a crash between steps must not leak a
  reservation or double-charge — persist saga state and make steps replayable.
- **No lost updates.** Concurrent stock/balance mutations need DB-level safety
  (atomic `UPDATE ... SET x = x ± ?`, `@Version`, or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`).
- **Durability.** State must live in Postgres, not memory — services can be
  restarted at any time and must recover committed state.
- **Eventual consistency.** Cross-service reads (stats, notifications) may lag;
  converge within the deadline.

The single-service GUIDE.md/EXAMPLE.md patterns (transactions, locking,
idempotency keys, async) all apply — now you also own the cross-service edges.

1	# Spring Boot 3.5 — Reference Pack (web + data-jpa)
2	
3	Terse reference for building a transactional REST backend on Spring Boot 3.5.14
4	(Java 25, Maven, PostgreSQL) with async processing, idempotency, lock-safe
5	concurrent writes, and eventually-consistent derived views. Code-heavy.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Core concepts
10	
11	### 1.1 Stack
12	- `spring-boot-starter-web` — Spring MVC, embedded Tomcat, Jackson.
13	- `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` — Hibernate 6.x (ORM 6), `JpaRepository`,
14	  `@Transactional`, HikariCP datasource.
15	- `spring-boot-starter-actuator` — `/actuator/health`, `/actuator/metrics`.
16	- PostgreSQL JDBC driver (runtime).
17	
18	### 1.2 Transactional consistency
19	- A `@Transactional` method runs in one DB transaction; on a thrown
20	  **unchecked** exception (RuntimeException/Error) it rolls back; on a **checked**
21	  exception it commits unless you set `rollbackFor`.
22	- Default isolation = the DB default (PostgreSQL = `READ_COMMITTED`).
23	- Postgres never blocks readers; concurrent writers to the **same row** block on
24	  row locks; writers to **different rows** under `READ_COMMITTED` do not see each
25	  other until commit — hence the need for explicit locking or atomic UPDATEs to
26	  avoid lost updates.
27	
28	### 1.3 Optimistic vs pessimistic locking
29	
30	**Optimistic (`@Version`).** Add a version column; Hibernate appends
31	`WHERE id=? AND version=?` and `SET version=version+1` to every UPDATE. If the
32	row changed since you read it, 0 rows match → `OptimisticLockException` /
33	Spring `ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException`. No DB locks held; you must
34	**retry**. Best when contention is low.
35	
36	```java
37	@Version
38	private long version;   // long or @Version Long / int / Integer / Timestamp
39	```
40	
41	**Pessimistic (`@Lock` / `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`).** Acquire a row lock at read
42	time so concurrent writers block until you commit. Best when contention is high
43	or the check-then-act window must be serialized (e.g. stock reservation).
44	
45	```java
46	@Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)            // SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
47	@Query("select p from Product p where p.id = :id")
48	Optional<Product> findByIdForUpdate(@Param("id") UUID id);
49	```
50	
51	`LockModeType` values: `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` (FOR UPDATE), `PESSIMISTIC_READ`
52	(FOR SHARE), `OPTIMISTIC`, `OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT`.
53	
54	### 1.4 Atomic UPDATE for lost-update-free increments
55	Read-modify-write (`x = read(); x += n; save();`) loses updates under
56	concurrency. Push the arithmetic into the DB so the row lock is held for the
57	whole operation:
58	
59	```java
60	@Modifying
61	@Query("update Product p set p.stock = p.stock + :units where p.id = :id")
62	int addStock(@Param("id") UUID id, @Param("units") int units);
63	```
64	
65	`SET stock = stock + ?` is atomic at the row level: concurrent calls serialize on
66	the row lock and **all** apply. Use the same shape for deposits
67	(`balance = balance + ?`). For conditional consumption (never negative), guard in
68	the WHERE clause and check the affected-row count:
69	
70	```java
71	@Modifying
72	@Query("update Product p set p.stock = p.stock - :q where p.id = :id and p.stock >= :q")
73	int tryReserve(@Param("id") UUID id, @Param("q") int q);  // returns 1 if reserved, 0 if insufficient
74	```
75	
76	### 1.5 Unique constraints for idempotency keys
77	A client-supplied id (order id) is an idempotency key. Make it the PK or a column
78	with a `UNIQUE` constraint. The DB rejects a duplicate INSERT with a unique
79	violation, surfaced as `DataIntegrityViolationException`. Catch it and treat as
80	"already seen" → no second insert, no second side effect. This is race-free even
81	under concurrent inserts, because uniqueness is enforced by the DB.
82	
83	### 1.6 Async processing
84	`@EnableAsync` + `@Async` runs a method on a `TaskExecutor` thread, returning
85	immediately (`void` or `CompletableFuture<T>`). Lets `POST /orders` return `202`
86	while processing happens in the background. Define a bounded executor; do not rely
87	on the default `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor` (unbounded threads) in production.
88	
89	```java
90	@Configuration
91	@EnableAsync
92	class AsyncConfig {
93	  @Bean ThreadPoolTaskExecutor taskExecutor() {
94	    var ex = new ThreadPoolTaskExecutor();
95	    ex.setCorePoolSize(4); ex.setMaxPoolSize(8); ex.setQueueCapacity(1000);
96	    ex.setThreadNamePrefix("worker-"); ex.initialize();
97	    return ex;
98	  }
99	}
100	```
101	
102	### 1.7 `@Transactional` semantics & pitfalls
103	- **Proxy self-invocation.** `@Transactional`/`@Async` work via a proxy. Calling
104	  another method **on `this`** bypasses the proxy → the annotation is ignored.
105	  Call through an injected bean (self-inject or split into another bean).
106	- `@Transactional` only applies to **public** methods on Spring-managed beans.
107	- The transaction commits when the **outer** annotated method returns; an
108	  `@Async` method starts a **new** thread with **no** inherited transaction.
109	- `propagation = REQUIRES_NEW` suspends the current tx and runs an independent
110	  one (useful to commit a record even if the caller rolls back).
111	
112	### 1.8 Retry on serialization / optimistic failures
113	Optimistic conflicts and serialization failures (`SQLState 40001`) are
114	**transient**: retry the whole transaction. Use Spring Retry or a manual loop;
115	each attempt must re-read inside a fresh transaction.
116	
117	```java
118	for (int attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
119	  try { return self.doInTx(...); }                 // self = proxied bean
120	  catch (ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException | CannotAcquireLockException e) {
121	    if (attempt >= 5) throw e;
122	  }
123	}
124	```
125	
126	---
127	
128	## 2. API reference (exact signatures)
129	
130	### Web (org.springframework.web.bind.annotation)
131	```java
132	@RestController
133	@RequestMapping("/orders")
134	class OrderController {
135	  @PostMapping
136	  @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.ACCEPTED)                       // 202
137	  OrderView create(@RequestBody @Valid CreateOrder body) { ... }
138	
139	  @GetMapping("/{id}")
140	  OrderView get(@PathVariable UUID id) { ... }
141	}
142	```
143	- `@RestController` = `@Controller` + `@ResponseBody`.
144	- `@RequestBody T` — Jackson-deserialize JSON body to `T`.
145	- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@Valid` (Jakarta Bean Validation).
146	- Throw `new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "reason")`
147	  (`org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException`) for 404/400.
148	- Map duplicate-key to 200/202 idempotent response, not 500.
149	
150	### Data JPA (org.springframework.data.jpa.repository)
151	```java
152	public interface ProductRepository extends JpaRepository<Product, UUID> {
153	  @Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)
154	  @Query("select p from Product p where p.id = :id")
155	  Optional<Product> findByIdForUpdate(@Param("id") UUID id);
156	
157	  @Modifying
158	  @Query("update Product p set p.stock = p.stock + :u where p.id = :id")
159	  int addStock(@Param("id") UUID id, @Param("u") int u);
160	}
161	```
162	- `JpaRepository<T,ID>`: `save`, `saveAndFlush`, `findById`, `getReferenceById`,

165	  Add `@Modifying(clearAutomatically = true, flushAutomatically = true)` if you
166	  read the same entity again in the same tx.

168	- `@Transactional(isolation = Isolation.SERIALIZABLE)` /

172	### Events (transactional, exactly-once-ish dispatch)
173	```java
174	// org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisher
175	publisher.publishEvent(new OrderDecided(orderId, status));
176	
177	// org.springframework.transaction.event.{TransactionalEventListener, TransactionPhase}
178	@TransactionalEventListener(phase = TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT)
179	void onDecided(OrderDecided e) { ... }   // fires only if the tx committed
180	```

182	  `AFTER_ROLLBACK`, `AFTER_COMPLETION`.
183	- `AFTER_COMMIT` guarantees the listener never sees an event whose tx rolled
184	  back. To also **persist** in the listener, annotate it
185	  `@Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW)` (the original tx is already
186	  committed/closed).
187	- For true exactly-once side effects, gate on a committed DB state transition
188	  (see §4) rather than relying on the event alone.
189	
190	### Exception handling
191	```java
192	// org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException  (wraps unique violations)
193	try { repo.save(order); }
194	catch (DataIntegrityViolationException dup) { /* idempotent: already exists */ }
195	
196	@RestControllerAdvice
197	class Errors {
198	  @ExceptionHandler(ResponseStatusException.class)
199	  ResponseEntity<?> rse(ResponseStatusException e) {
200	    return ResponseEntity.status(e.getStatusCode()).body(Map.of("error", e.getReason()));
201	  }
202	}
203	```
204	- `MethodArgumentNotValidException` / `HttpMessageNotReadableException` → 400
205	  (handled by Spring Boot's default error mapping; override via `@ExceptionHandler`).
206	
207	---
208	
209	## 3. Wiring (application.properties)
210	
211	```properties
212	server.port=${PORT:8080}
213	spring.datasource.url=${DB_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/app}
214	spring.datasource.username=${DB_USER:postgres}
215	spring.datasource.password=${DB_PASS:secret}
216	
217	# Hibernate schema generation (skeleton uses 'update'; never use in real prod)
218	spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
219	spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.jdbc.time_zone=UTC
220	
221	# HikariCP (pool sizing must exceed async worker count to avoid starvation)
222	spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=15
223	spring.datasource.hikari.minimum-idle=5
224	spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=10000
225	
226	# Actuator
227	management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,metrics
228	management.endpoint.health.show-details=never
229	```
230	- DDL `update` adds tables/columns from `@Entity` mappings; it does NOT add
231	  arbitrary `UNIQUE`/`CHECK` constraints unless declared via `@Table`/`@Column`.
232	  Declare idempotency uniqueness in the entity (see §4) so it is created.
233	- Pool sizing: a request thread + the async worker may each need a connection;
234	  size Hikari so worker pool + expected concurrent web requests fit.
235	
236	---
237	
238	## 4. Worked mini-flow
239	
240	Pattern: `POST /orders` inserts a PENDING row (idempotent via PK), returns 202,
241	and dispatches async work. The worker does the saga (reserve → charge →
242	confirm/reject+release) and is **exactly-once** because every side effect is
243	gated by a committed status transition `PENDING → CONFIRMED|REJECTED` guarded in
244	the WHERE clause: only the first thread to flip it from PENDING proceeds.
245	
246	### Entity with @Version (optimistic) + atomic counters
247	```java
248	@Entity @Table(name = "product")
249	class Product {
250	  @Id UUID id;
251	  String name;
252	  int unitPrice;
253	  int stock;
254	  @Version long version;
255	}
256	```
257	
258	### Repository: atomic, conditional, lost-update-free
259	```java
260	public interface ProductRepository extends JpaRepository<Product, UUID> {
261	  @Modifying
262	  @Query("update Product p set p.stock = p.stock + :u where p.id = :id")
263	  int restock(@Param("id") UUID id, @Param("u") int u);
264	
265	  @Modifying
266	  @Query("update Product p set p.stock = p.stock - :q where p.id = :id and p.stock >= :q")
267	  int reserve(@Param("id") UUID id, @Param("q") int q);   // 1 = ok, 0 = OUT_OF_STOCK
268	}
269	```
270	
271	### Service: idempotent create + safe check-then-act
272	```java
273	@Service
274	class OrderService {
275	  private final OrderRepository orders; private final ProductRepository products;
276	  private final CustomerRepository customers; private final OrderService self; // proxied self
277	  // ... constructor; self injected via @Lazy to call @Async/@Transactional through the proxy
278	
279	  @Transactional
280	  public OrderView create(CreateOrder cmd) {
281	    if (orders.existsById(cmd.orderId())) return view(orders.findById(cmd.orderId()).get());
282	    try {
283	      orders.saveAndFlush(new Order(cmd.orderId(), cmd.customerId(),
284	                                    cmd.productId(), cmd.quantity(), Status.PENDING));
285	    } catch (DataIntegrityViolationException dup) {           // concurrent duplicate
286	      return view(orders.findById(cmd.orderId()).orElseThrow());
287	    }
288	    self.processAsync(cmd.orderId());                          // through proxy → real @Async
289	    return new OrderView(cmd.orderId(), Status.PENDING);
290	  }
291	
292	  @Async
293	  public void processAsync(UUID orderId) { self.process(orderId); }   // tx starts in process()
294	
295	  @Transactional
296	  public void process(UUID orderId) {
297	    Order o = orders.findById(orderId).orElseThrow();
298	    if (o.status != Status.PENDING) return;                   // already decided → no-op (idempotent)
299	    int total = o.quantity * products.findById(o.productId).orElseThrow().unitPrice;
300	
301	    if (products.reserve(o.productId, o.quantity) == 0) { decide(o, Status.REJECTED, "OUT_OF_STOCK"); return; }
302	    if (customers.charge(o.customerId, total) == 0) {         // charge = balance-:t where balance>=:t
303	      products.restock(o.productId, o.quantity);              // COMPENSATION: release reservation
304	      decide(o, Status.REJECTED, "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS"); return;
305	    }
306	    decide(o, Status.CONFIRMED, null);                        // sets total too
307	  }
308	
309	  private void decide(Order o, Status s, String reason) {
310	    o.status = s; o.reason = reason;                          // optimistic @Version protects against double-decide
311	    orders.save(o);
312	    publisher.publishEvent(new OrderDecided(o.id, s));        // notification fired AFTER_COMMIT
313	  }
314	}
315	```
316	
317	### Exactly-once notification via AFTER_COMMIT + committed-state guard
318	The `process` method is a no-op when status is not PENDING, so even if `@Async`
319	retries or runs twice, only the first committed transition emits a decision. The
320	`@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)` then writes exactly one notification
321	row. Make the notification table carry a `UNIQUE(orderId)` so a re-delivered
322	event is deduplicated by the DB:
323	
324	```java
325	@TransactionalEventListener(phase = TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT)
326	@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW)
327	void notify(OrderDecided e) {
328	  try { notifications.saveAndFlush(new Notification(e.orderId(), e.status())); }
329	  catch (DataIntegrityViolationException already) { /* exactly-once: skip */ }
330	}
331	```
332	
333	### Eventually-consistent stats view
334	Stats (`confirmed`, `rejected`, `revenue`) are **derived**. Either compute on
335	read with an aggregate query, or maintain a counters row updated atomically in
336	the same committed transition. Reads may lag writes by up to the convergence
337	window; that is acceptable for an eventually-consistent view.
338	
339	```java
340	@Query("select new com.study.app.query.Stats(" +
341	       " sum(case when o.status='CONFIRMED' then 1 else 0 end)," +
342	       " sum(case when o.status='REJECTED'  then 1 else 0 end)," +
343	       " coalesce(sum(case when o.status='CONFIRMED' then o.total else 0 end),0)) from Order o")
344	Stats stats();
345	```
346	
347	---
348	
349	## 5. Common pitfalls
350	
351	1. **Lost updates from read-modify-write.** `e = find(); e.setStock(e.getStock()+n); save();`
352	   loses concurrent increments. Use atomic `UPDATE ... SET x = x + ?` (§1.4) or
353	   pessimistic lock the row first.
354	2. **Overselling / negative balance.** Guard consumption in the WHERE clause
355	   (`... where stock >= :q`) and branch on the affected-row count; do not read
356	   then subtract.
357	3. **Double-processing without an idempotency key.** Without a UNIQUE on the
358	   client order id, a retried `POST /orders` creates a second order and charges
359	   twice. Use the order id as PK / UNIQUE and catch
360	   `DataIntegrityViolationException`.
361	4. **Proxy self-invocation.** `this.process(...)` from within the same bean
362	   ignores `@Async`/`@Transactional`. Inject the proxied self (`@Lazy`) or split
363	   into a separate bean.
364	5. **`@Async` + `@Transactional` interplay.** The async method runs on a new
365	   thread with **no** ambient transaction; start the transaction *inside* the
366	   async method (or in a method it calls through the proxy). An entity loaded in
367	   the caller's tx is detached in the worker — re-load by id.
368	6. **Listener can't see the row it reacts to.** With `AFTER_COMMIT`, the
369	   committing tx is closed; a `@TransactionalEventListener` that writes must use
370	   `REQUIRES_NEW`, and should re-load entities by id.
371	7. **Eventual consistency of derived views.** Don't assert read-your-writes on
372	   stats/notifications immediately; allow the convergence window and converge via
373	   committed transitions, not in-memory state.
374	8. **Connection-pool starvation.** Async workers + web threads competing for a
375	   too-small Hikari pool deadlock. Size the pool above worker count.

## Summary

I implemented the collaborative todo-list system as **four independent Spring Boot services** (the Maven reactor's `edge`, `lists`, `items`, `notifications`), each its own deployable, three with their own Postgres database, integrating purely over HTTP/REST — no broker, no CQRS/event-sourcing/messaging dependencies. **`make test` passes all 20 acceptance tests** (contract, lifecycle, and concurrency), in ~9s.

### Service decomposition & data ownership
- **edge** (stateless): the public REST contract. Forwards writes to the owning service (propagating the downstream status), and composes cross-service reads — `GET /lists/{id}` merges the lists summary with items; `GET /stats/lists` merges `{active,completed}` from lists with `{totalItems,checkedItems}` from items.
- **lists**: authoritative list identity + `ACTIVE/COMPLETED` status; owns the completion-transition detection and stats counts. On create it synchronously registers the list with items and notifications so immediate follow-up item ops don't 404.
- **items**: items (`content`, `checked`) keyed by `(listId, itemId)`; computes list completeness and reports edges to lists.
- **notifications**: one record per completion transition.

### How the hard requirements are met (no broker — built by hand)
- **Exactly-once completion under a concurrent final check**: every item mutation runs under a **per-list pessimistic row lock** (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on a `list_ref` row) in the items service, so the "are all items checked?" decision is serialized. The last writer is the only one that observes the false→true edge, so completeness flips to `true` exactly once.
- **Reliable, idempotent cross-service delivery via transactional outbox**: items writes a completeness report to an outbox in the same tx as the mutation; a dispatcher delivers it at-least-once to lists, which applies it under a per-list lock with a **monotonic seq guard** (rejects stale/duplicate reports) and detects the `ACTIVE↔COMPLETED` transitions. On each `ACTIVE→COMPLETED` edge, lists writes a notification-outbox row (same tx) → dispatched to notifications, which dedupes on `UNIQUE(listId, transitionSeq)`. Net effect: **exactly one notification per transition, never zero, never two**, under retries and concurrency.
- **Idempotency**: client-supplied UUIDs are primary keys; concurrent first-creates race on the INSERT and the loser catches `DataIntegrityViolationException`.
- **No lost update (rename vs check)**: mutations use targeted column `UPDATE`s (`SET checked=…` / `SET content=…`) rather than whole-entity saves, so concurrent rename and check both survive.
- **Durability / restart survival**: all business state (lists, items, checked state, status, notifications, and both outboxes) lives in Postgres; dispatchers resume on boot — verified above.
- **Eventual consistency**: views converge within the deadline via the 100ms outbox dispatchers; invalid/non-UUID ids resolve to `404` (not `400`) on read/update paths, and validation returns `400`.

Code follows the prescribed `com.study.app.{web,command,query,domain,config}` layering, and I changed no build coordinates, dependency constraints, or the pre-wired skeleton config (only appended Hikari pool sizing). `.run-env` and the acceptance tests were left untouched.
